results.cause: The pod spec runs command ["/app/payment-gateway", "--listen=:8443"] on image "busybox:1.36", a stock BusyBox image with no /app/payment-gateway binary. The runtime reports: exec: "/app/payment-gateway": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory (StartError, exit 128). The rule finding says exit 127, but the actual code is 128 (StartError). The cause is the same: the command is not in the image. The image field most likely points at a placeholder instead of the real payment-gateway image.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image in deployment/payment-gateway to the image that actually contains /app/payment-gateway (your built payment-gateway image), e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<your-payment-gateway-image>:<tag>`.
If the image is correct but the binary lives at a different path, change the container's command to that path.
After updating, check rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/payment-gateway` (the ProgressDeadlineExceeded condition clears on a new rollout).

results.cause: The migrate init container's script is hardcoded to fail. Its args echo "applying migration 0042_add_orders_index", then write 'ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists' to stderr and run 'exit 1'. It can never succeed as written. In a real migration, this error means the migration is not idempotent: the index orders_idx already exists, so re-running 0042 fails and blocks the pod.
fix: Change the migrate init container's args (spec.template.spec.initContainers[name=migrate].args) so the script exits 0 on success. Remove the unconditional 'exit 1'.

If this stands in for a real migration, make 0042_add_orders_index idempotent (e.g. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ...). Otherwise mark the migration as already applied in the migration tracking table.
Apply the updated Deployment (kubectl apply -f <manifest> -n pfa-lab) and confirm migrate completes and api starts: kubectl get pod -n pfa-lab -l app=orders-api -w

results.known_gap: The crash rule quotes the last error line in the logs. Here that is the statsd flush during shutdown, not the fatal config error before it.
results.cause: The fatal config error is MAX_CONNECTIONS: the log says level=fatal msg="config: MAX_CONNECTIONS=\"ten\" is not an integer", followed by "shutting down" and exit code 1. The low-certainty rule finding points at the statsd flush error, but that line only appears during shutdown, after the fatal. The redis:6379 connection refused error is non-fatal because the app falls back to in-memory caching.
fix: Set the MAX_CONNECTIONS env var on container api in deployment/pricing-api to an integer, e.g. "10" instead of "ten". If it comes from a ConfigMap or Secret, fix the value there. Example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/pricing-api -c api MAX_CONNECTIONS=10
If the value comes from a ConfigMap or Secret, restart the pods after updating it: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/pricing-api
Optionally, make redis:6379 (CACHE_URL) and statsd:8125 (STATSD_ADDR) reachable. Neither causes the crash, but the pod currently runs without a shared cache or metrics.

results.cause: The startup script requires DATABASE_URL and exits 1 when it is empty. The log says "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set", and the container env only has DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL. Separately, the script echoes DB_PASSWORD to stdout, so a password value appears in the logs (redacted here).
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env of deployment/checkout-api in namespace pfa-lab. If the URL contains credentials, source it from a Secret, e.g. `env: - name: DATABASE_URL valueFrom: secretKeyRef: {name: <secret>, key: <key>}`.
Apply the change, then check the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api`.
Remove `password=$DB_PASSWORD` from the startup echo so the password is no longer written to logs, and rotate that password since it has already been logged.

results.known_gap: The cause quotes the right log line, but no rule recognises a failed DNS lookup of a Service name, so the fix is generic.
results.cause: DB_HOST is set to "orders-db", but cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) has no record for it: "FATAL: db: dial tcp: lookup orders-db on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host". Either no Service named orders-db exists in namespace pfa-lab, or the database runs in another namespace and needs a qualified name (e.g. orders-db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local). The start script exits 1 when nslookup of $DB_HOST fails.
fix: Check whether the Service exists: kubectl get svc -n pfa-lab orders-db; kubectl get svc -A | grep orders-db

If the database Service lives in another namespace or has another name, set the DB_HOST env var on container api to the correct name, e.g. <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local, then roll out: kubectl set env deployment/shipping-api -n pfa-lab -c api DB_HOST=<correct-host>
If the database was never deployed, deploy it with a Service named orders-db in pfa-lab. The pod will recover on its next restart.

results.known_gap: The rules diagnose one container, the most broken one; the worker's failure is never mentioned.
results.cause: The api startup script checks for REDIS_URL and exits 1 when it is empty. The log shows "FATAL: required environment variable REDIS_URL is not set", and the container env only has ["PORT"], so REDIS_URL is not defined. Separately, the worker container in the same pod also crashes (exit code 2, "error: open /etc/cart/worker.yaml: no such file or directory"), so the pod stays unready even after api is fixed.
fix: Add REDIS_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env in deployment/cart-service. If it holds credentials, use valueFrom.secretKeyRef, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/cart-service -c api --from=secret/<redis-secret>`, or set it directly with `kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/cart-service -c api REDIS_URL=<redis url>`.
Fix the worker container too: mount a ConfigMap or volume that provides /etc/cart/worker.yaml (volumeMounts mountPath /etc/cart), otherwise the pod will never become Ready.
Let the rollout finish and verify with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/cart-service`.

results.cause: The registry answered "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found". The tag "1.36.1-uclbic" appears to be a typo of "1.36.1-uclibc" ("uclbic" vs "uclibc"), so the image reference does not exist.
fix: Correct the tag in spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc`.
Confirm the corrected tag exists before rolling out: `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` (or `crane ls busybox`).
Watch the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront`.

results.cause: The image field has two tags: "busybox:1.36:latest". A reference can have only one ":tag", so the kubelet rejects it with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). This is not a registry or credentials problem. The likely cause is a template or tag variable appending ":latest" to an image that already has a tag.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=worker].image in deployment/notify-worker to a single-tag reference, e.g. "busybox:1.36": kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36
If the image string is built from variables (e.g. Helm/Kustomize image + tag), fix the source so the tag is not appended to a value that already contains one.
Watch the rollout recover (it currently shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded): kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/notify-worker

results.cause: Docker Hub answers NotFound for the tag: "docker.io/library/busybox:1.63: not found". The tag 1.63 does not exist for busybox, most likely a typo or nonexistent version. The FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret warning for "regcred" is a side issue. busybox is a public image and the error is NotFound, not unauthorized, so the missing secret is not what blocks the pull.
fix: Change the container image to an existing busybox tag (for example a real 1.36.x tag; check with `docker manifest inspect busybox:<tag>` or `crane ls busybox`) and redeploy, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/admin-portal web=busybox:<valid-tag>`.
Either remove the unused `imagePullSecrets: [regcred]` from the pod spec or create the secret `regcred` in namespace pfa-lab, so the FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret warning goes away.
Watch the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/admin-portal`.

results.cause: The node pulls through the registry mirror registry-mirror:1273, and the mirror answered the manifest request with "500 Internal Server Error" (HEAD http://registry-mirror:1273/v2/billing/ui/manifests/3.2.0?ns=registry.pfa-lab.invalid). The mirror could not fetch the image from upstream registry.pfa-lab.invalid. The most likely reason is that this registry hostname is wrong or unreachable from the mirror; the ".invalid" TLD is reserved and never resolves. Less likely, the mirror itself is failing. This is not a tag or auth error: the registry returned neither 'not found' nor 'unauthorized'.
fix: Correct the registry hostname in the image reference. For example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<correct-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0, or edit spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image in the manifest.

If registry.pfa-lab.invalid is intended, make sure the mirror registry-mirror:1273 can resolve and reach it. Check the mirror's logs and upstream/proxy configuration, and fix the mirror if it is returning 500 for every request.
After fixing, restart the rollout (kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/billing-ui) and confirm with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/billing-ui.

results.cause: The container command runs "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0", which allocates 300M, but resources.limits.memory is 200Mi. The logs show warmup reaching "cache warmup: loading remaining 100MB" and "stress: info: [1] dispatching hogs: 0 cpu, 0 io, 1 vm, 0 hdd", after which the container terminates with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, about 8s after start (14:29:10 to 14:29:18). The app's intended working set (~300MB) simply does not fit in 200Mi.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) on container cache in statefulset/session-cache to fit the 300M allocation plus overhead, e.g. 384Mi: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"384Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"384Mi"}]'
Alternatively, if 200Mi must stay, reduce usage: lower --vm-bytes in the container args to well under 200M (e.g. 150M).
If the pod does not restart automatically after the change, delete it so the StatefulSet recreates it with the new spec: kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pod session-cache-0

results.cause: The container runs "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0" and logs "loading 250MB of order history into memory", but resources.limits.memory is 128Mi. Allocating ~250MB (about 238Mi, plus process overhead) exceeds the limit almost immediately, so it is terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory on container worker to at least 320Mi (e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=320Mi --requests=memory=256Mi`). This leaves headroom above the 250M allocation.
Alternatively reduce usage: lower --vm-bytes (or make the real app load order history in smaller batches) so peak memory stays well under 128Mi.
Raise requests.memory (currently 64Mi) close to the real usage, e.g. 256Mi, so the scheduler places the pod on a node that actually has the memory.

results.cause: The container command allocates far more memory than its limit: args run "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0" (log line "buffering 200MB of logs in memory"), but resources.limits.memory is 64Mi. It hits the limit right away and is terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137 (started and finished at 2026-11-11T14:28:46). This is a fixed oversize allocation, not a leak. Raising the limit to 128Mi as the generic rule suggests would still be too low.
fix: Either reduce the allocation to fit the limit, e.g. change --vm-bytes 200M to a value well under 64Mi (such as 32M) in the log-shipper args, or raise the log-shipper limit to cover the 200M allocation plus headroom.

To raise the limit, set resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) to at least 256Mi, e.g.: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi
For a real log shipper, configure a bounded in-memory buffer (or spill to disk) so usage stays below the memory limit.

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores), almost certainly a unit typo for "4000m" (4 cores). The scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu" and preemption cannot help.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu from "4k"/"4000" to "4000m", or a smaller value the app actually needs (e.g. "500m" for this busybox sleep), for example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m
Make sure the corrected request fits within the node's allocatable CPU (kubectl describe node). If 4 cores is more than the node can offer, lower the request further or add a larger node.
After the rollout, confirm the new pod schedules: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ml-trainer

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab. The kubelet keeps failing with "MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume \"templates\" : configmap \"email-templates\" not found" (1063 times since 2026-11-02), so the container never starts and the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the right namespace, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>`. The kubelet retries the mount and the pod should start on its own.

If the configmap exists under another name or in another namespace, fix `spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.name` in deployment/email-sender to the correct name. Create it in pfa-lab if it only exists elsewhere.
If the templates are optional, set `spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.optional: true` so the pod can start without the configmap.
After fixing, check the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/email-sender`. Run `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/email-sender` if the pod does not recover.

results.cause: The pod spec sets nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, and the scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (120 FailedScheduling events). No node carries the label hardware=gpu-a100. Preemption cannot help, and the Deployment has hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: If the container does not need a GPU node (it runs busybox:1.36 'sleep 3600'), remove the nodeSelector: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
Or set spec.template.spec.nodeSelector to a label that exists on your node. Check the labels with: kubectl get nodes --show-labels
Or, if the node really is the intended A100 host, label it: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
If the workload truly needs an A100 node, add one to the cluster with the label hardware=gpu-a100.

results.known_gap: pfa reads only the pod's and its owners' events. The reason (StorageClass fast-ssd not found) is on the PersistentVolumeClaim, which pfa cannot read.
results.cause: The scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims. not found". The trailing "not found" suggests the PVC metrics-data does not exist in namespace pfa-lab, though this is not confirmed. The other possibility is that it exists but has no matching PersistentVolume or StorageClass to bind it.
fix: Run `kubectl -n pfa-lab get pvc metrics-data`. If it is missing, create it: a PersistentVolumeClaim named metrics-data in namespace pfa-lab with accessModes, resources.requests.storage, and a valid storageClassName. Alternatively, fix the claimName in the Deployment's volumes if it is misspelled.

If the PVC exists but is Pending, check `kubectl -n pfa-lab describe pvc metrics-data`. Then make sure its storageClassName exists (`kubectl get storageclass`) and its provisioner is running, or create a matching PersistentVolume.
Once the PVC is Bound, the scheduler retries automatically. If the pod stays Pending, delete it so the ReplicaSet recreates it.

results.known_gap: The probe rules use the first failing probe event (connection refused, from before the server started), not the 503 that repeats.
results.cause: The readiness endpoint does a DNS lookup of DB_HOST, which is "inventory-db". The logs show "readiness: database inventory-db:5432 unreachable: lookup inventory-db: no such host", so the endpoint returns 503. No Service named inventory-db resolves from namespace pfa-lab: either the database Service does not exist, has a different name, or lives in another namespace and needs a qualified name. The single "connection refused" event at 14:31:28 was only the first probe firing before httpd started. The app does listen on :80, so the probe_app_not_listening finding is not the real cause.
fix: Check whether the database Service exists: kubectl get svc -A | grep inventory-db
If it is missing, deploy the database and its Service named inventory-db in namespace pfa-lab.
If it lives in another namespace, set the DB_HOST env var on container api to the qualified name, e.g. inventory-db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local.
If it has a different name, set DB_HOST to the correct Service name, then roll out: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/stock-api

results.cause: The readiness probe is configured as "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves /healthz: the startup command writes only /www/healthz and the log says "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz". httpd returns 404 for /ready (event: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404", x43754). The port is correct (http=80/TCP, app listens on :80); only the path is wrong.
fix: Change the readiness probe path in the deployment: spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path from /ready to /healthz (keep port: http).
Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]'
Alternatively, if /ready must stay, make the app serve it (e.g. add 'echo ok > /www/ready' to the container args).

results.cause: The app sleeps ~45s replaying its journal before starting httpd on port 80 (log: "ledger-api replaying journal, this takes about 45 seconds"), but the liveness probe starts after initialDelaySeconds=2 with periodSeconds=3 and failureThreshold=2, so it gives up after roughly 5-8s. Probes to http://10.244.0.16:80/healthz get "connection refused", the kubelet kills the container (exit code 137), and the "ledger-api listening on :80" line is never reached. The probe's port and path (http=80, /healthz) match what the app will serve, so the only problem is timing.
fix: Add a startupProbe to container api that covers the 45s startup, e.g. httpGet path /healthz port http, periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 18 (about 90s budget). The liveness probe only runs after the startupProbe succeeds.
Alternatively, raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to at least 60 (above the 45s journal replay), and consider failureThreshold: 3 and timeoutSeconds: 2.
Optionally add a readinessProbe on /healthz port http so traffic is only sent once httpd is listening.
Apply the change (kubectl -n pfa-lab apply or edit deployment/ledger-api) and confirm the logs show "ledger-api listening on :80" and the restart count stops increasing.

results.cause: The liveness probe is "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80", logs "inventory-api listening on :80" and declares only port http=80/TCP. Every probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused". After failure_threshold 2 at period 3s, the kubelet kills the container (exit code 137) even though it did not crash.
fix: In the statefulset inventory-api pod template, change spec.containers[name=api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port from 8080 to 80 (or to the named port "http").

Apply the change, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'. If the pod is not replaced automatically, delete it with kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pod inventory-api-0.
Optionally relax the probe (for example timeoutSeconds > 1, failureThreshold > 2) so short hiccups do not trigger restarts.
